purpose: LLM-ready codebook for classifying MCP servers into the eight paper categories. Agent-oriented and miscellaneous servers are not separate top-level classes; classify them by dominant exposed user-facing function.
evidence_priority: Exposed MCP tool/resource/prompt names and descriptions
README feature, capability, and available-tools sections
Package metadata description, keywords, dependencies, scripts, and service names
Configuration variables that reveal an external service or domain
Repository name only when stronger evidence is unavailable
noise_to_ignore: Generic MCP, Claude Desktop, Cursor, VS Code, or client setup text
Installation commands such as npm install, pip install, uv run, docker run, git clone, or npx
Repository hosting metadata such as homepage, bugs URL, license, badges, or contribution instructions
Generic authentication setup unless identity, permission, secrets, or access control is the core exposed capability
Dockerfile, CI, tests, or deployment instructions unless the exposed MCP tools manage infrastructure
global_decision_rules: Classify by dominant exposed capability, not by implementation language, installation method, framework, or generic MCP protocol integration.
If tool names and README disagree, prefer tool names because they represent the server's callable interface.
If a server exposes multiple capabilities, choose the category that captures the highest-value user-facing operation, not incidental support functions.

Agent, copilot, AI, LLM, prompt, memory, or RAG wording is not a category by itself. Assign by what the server lets the user do: retrieve knowledge, run commands, manage repositories, create tasks, analyze media, and so on.
Do not assign to Source Control solely because a README or package metadata contains a GitHub repository URL.
Do not assign to Infrastructure solely because a Dockerfile, docker run command, or CI badge appears in installation documentation.
Do not assign to Security solely because a server requires an API key, OAuth token, or secure connection.
When evidence is sparse, assign the closest paper category using concrete service/domain clues; do not invent an Other category.

tie_breakers.condition: A server retrieves data from a database, documentation site, search engine, wiki, public API, or SaaS record store without primarily changing external state.
A server controls cloud resources, containers, deployments, proxies, gateways, monitoring, logs, incidents, or service lifecycle.
A server creates or manages commits, branches, repository files, pull/merge requests, releases, diffs, reviews, or source-hosting repositories.
A server executes shell commands, scripts, local filesystem operations, browser automation, desktop automation, screenshots, scraping, or local workspace control.
A server manages tasks, todos, tickets, calendars, meetings, reminders, email, chat, team messages, or workflow coordination.
A server handles payments, orders, invoices, banking, trading, portfolios, ecommerce, wallets, smart contracts, tokens, NFTs, or on-chain data.

A server performs computation, statistics, analysis, reporting, visualization, media generation/editing, design, transcription, QR generation, camera/hardware/peripheral interaction, or AI generation that is not primarily knowledge retrieval.
A server performs vulnerability scanning, penetration testing, CVE/threat intelligence, security audit, IAM, secrets, vaults, policy, permissions, compliance, or access-control management.

categories.name: Data and Public Content Access
categories.short_description: Retrieval of data, knowledge, and public content.
categories.definition: Servers whose primary function is to retrieve, query, search, summarize, or expose structured data, documents, knowledge bases, web content, public content, or SaaS records.
include: Database and warehouse querying: SQL, Postgres, MySQL, SQLite, MongoDB, Elasticsearch, BigQuery, Snowflake, Supabase, Kusto, Redis query interfaces
Knowledge and document retrieval: documentation, files-as-knowledge, PDFs, papers, arXiv, wiki, Notion, Obsidian, Confluence, Google Drive/Docs read access
Web and public-content search: Google/Bing/Brave/Exa search, browserless content fetching, RSS, news, Wikipedia, YouTube transcript retrieval, public social content lookup
SaaS record lookup where the primary operation is read/search/list rather than task workflow or state-changing collaboration
RAG, embeddings, semantic search, memory, or vector search when the exposed capability is retrieving knowledge/context
exclude: Repository operations such as commits, branches, PRs, merge requests, repository files, releases, or code review
Cloud/database administration, deployments, container operations, gateway/proxy management, or observability operations
Financial trading, payments, ecommerce order/customer/product management, wallets, smart contracts, or on-chain analysis
Security scanning, CVE lookup, pentesting, IAM, secrets, policy, permission audit, or compliance
Local browser control, scraping automation, shell execution, or filesystem editing where automation/control is the main value
Computation, visualization, report generation, media processing, image/audio/video/design tools
positive_examples: A PostgreSQL MCP server exposing list_tables and query tools
A Notion or Obsidian MCP server exposing page search and document retrieval
A Brave Search or Wikipedia MCP server exposing web/public content lookup
A RAG documentation server exposing semantic search over local or hosted docs
negative_examples: A GitHub MCP server that reads repository files and creates pull requests: Source Control and Collaboration
A Stripe MCP server that retrieves customers and creates payments: Financial and Blockchain Services
A Playwright server that fetches pages through browser automation: Local Execution and Automation
A dashboard generator that computes and plots metrics: Analytics and Peripheral Tools

categories.name: Infrastructure and Gateway Services
categories.short_description: Container orchestration, infrastructure operations, and gateway proxying.
categories.definition: Servers whose primary function is to administer infrastructure, cloud resources, containers, deployments, service lifecycle, observability, gateways, proxies, or MCP/server orchestration.
include: Cloud administration: AWS, Azure, GCP, Cloudflare, Alibaba Cloud, Vercel, Netlify, Supabase management, DNS, certificates, storage buckets, serverless resources
Containers and orchestration: Docker, Docker Compose, Kubernetes, Helm, Terraform, container registries, image build/push, deployment lifecycle
DevOps and CI/CD operations when the server manages builds, pipelines, environments, deployments, releases, infrastructure state, or service operations
Observability and incident operations: logs, metrics, traces, monitoring, alerts, dashboards for service health, incident response
Gateways, proxies, routers, API gateways, MCP aggregators, MCP registries, tool routers, service mesh, request forwarding
exclude: Docker/CI/deployment text that appears only in installation instructions
Local shell execution or filesystem/browser automation without infrastructure control
Repository PR/commit/branch workflows without infrastructure operations
Task orchestration in project-management tools such as Jira, Linear, Trello, or calendars
Security audit of infrastructure when the main exposed function is vulnerability or compliance assessment
positive_examples: A Kubernetes MCP server exposing create_deployment, list_pods, and get_logs
A Cloudflare MCP server managing DNS records, certificates, and workers
An MCP gateway that routes tools across multiple backend MCP servers
A Grafana/Prometheus server exposing logs, metrics, and incident operations
negative_examples: A package with a Dockerfile only for installation: classify by exposed tools, not Infrastructure
A local command runner that happens to run docker commands supplied by the user: Local Execution and Automation
A GitHub Actions PR helper focused on repository workflows: Source Control and Collaboration
A security compliance scanner for cloud resources: Security, Access Control, and Scanning

categories.name: Source Control and Collaboration
categories.short_description: Repository management and collaborative development workflows.
categories.definition: Servers whose primary function is to manage source-code repositories and developer collaboration around code, including Git operations, repository files, branches, commits, pull/merge requests, code review, issues tied to repositories, and releases.
include: GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket, Gitea, Forgejo, Sourcegraph, or Azure DevOps repository APIs
Git operations: status, log, diff, add, checkout, branch, clone, commit, merge, pull, push, reset
Repository file workflows: create/update/delete/read repository files, compare diffs, list commits, browse repository trees
Pull request and merge request workflows: create, list, comment, review, approve, merge, decline, fetch diffs
Code review, PR description generation, commit message generation, repository release/tag management
Issue/project operations only when tightly coupled to repository collaboration or source-hosting platforms
exclude: Generic GitHub repository URL, homepage, badges, bugs link, or contribution instructions
Jira, Linear, Trello, Asana, or project-management tickets without repository operations
Cloud deployment or CI/CD service operations where infrastructure lifecycle is dominant
Security scanning of repositories, dependencies, secrets, or code vulnerabilities
Local filesystem editing or shell command execution unless it is specifically Git/source-control workflow
positive_examples: A GitHub server exposing create_pull_request, list_repositories, and get_file_contents
A GitLab MR review server exposing get_merge_request_diff and post_review_comment
A local Git assistant exposing git_diff, git_commit, git_push, and branch operations
A Bitbucket MCP server exposing PR comments, repository files, and commit history
negative_examples: A README says contributions are welcome on GitHub but tools are weather lookup: Data and Public Content Access
A Snyk server scans GitHub repositories for vulnerabilities: Security, Access Control, and Scanning
A Vercel server deploys a GitHub repo to production: Infrastructure and Gateway Services
A Jira-only issue tracker: Task and Schedule Management

categories.name: Local Execution and Automation
categories.short_description: Local command execution, script running, and automation.
categories.definition: Servers whose primary function is to execute commands, run scripts, manipulate local files/workspaces, automate browsers/desktops/UIs, capture screenshots, scrape via controlled browsers, or operate local development environments.
include: Shell, terminal, command execution, subprocess execution, Python/Node script execution, build/test/run command helpers
Filesystem operations: read/write/move/delete/search local files, directory trees, workspace context, local project editing
Browser and UI automation: Playwright, Puppeteer, Selenium, browser clicks, screenshots, forms, crawler, page interaction
Desktop or OS automation: clipboard, keyboard/mouse, window/app control, local environment detection, command syntax helpers
Local development automation not specifically tied to repository collaboration or cloud infrastructure
exclude: Cloud/container/service lifecycle management: Infrastructure and Gateway Services
Git PR/commit/branch/repository collaboration: Source Control and Collaboration
Public web search without browser/UI control: Data and Public Content Access
Security scanning using local tools when the dominant goal is vulnerability/security assessment
Task/calendar/email/chat workflow coordination
positive_examples: A filesystem MCP server exposing read_file and write_file
A terminal MCP server exposing run_command or execute_shell
A Playwright MCP server exposing browser_click, browser_fill_form, and screenshot
A development environment copilot that detects OS/shell and formats local commands
negative_examples: A Kubernetes server that executes kubectl-like cluster operations: Infrastructure and Gateway Services
A Git helper focused on commits and branches: Source Control and Collaboration
A web search API wrapper: Data and Public Content Access
An Nmap security scanner: Security, Access Control, and Scanning

categories.name: Task and Schedule Management
categories.short_description: Task orchestration, workflow coordination, and scheduling.
categories.definition: Servers whose primary function is to manage tasks, todos, calendars, schedules, reminders, meetings, tickets, project boards, email, team communication, or workflow coordination.
include: Tasks, todos, reminders, checklists, personal productivity, project boards, and workflow state
Calendar and scheduling: events, meetings, availability, free/busy, reminders, time slots, agenda management
Ticket and project-management systems: Jira, Linear, Trello, Asana, ClickUp, Monday, Taskwarrior, GitHub Projects when used as project management
Communication and collaboration: email, Gmail, Slack, Discord, Telegram, WhatsApp, Teams, message sending/reading, meeting notes
Workflow orchestration when the workflow is human/team/task coordination rather than infrastructure deployment
exclude: Repository commits, branches, pull/merge requests, code review, or repository releases
Public social-media search or content retrieval without user/team communication actions
Infrastructure workflow orchestration such as deployments, pipelines, service incidents, or cloud operations
Financial order/payment/customer workflows
Security incident, audit, or compliance workflows when security is dominant
positive_examples: A Google Calendar server exposing create_event and list_events
A Gmail or Slack server exposing send_message and search_messages
A Jira or Linear server exposing create_issue, assign_task, and update_status
A Taskwarrior server exposing add_task and list_tasks
negative_examples: A GitHub PR server with issue comments and repository branches: Source Control and Collaboration
A Twitter/X public search server: Data and Public Content Access
A CI/CD deployment workflow server: Infrastructure and Gateway Services
A Stripe order/payment workflow server: Financial and Blockchain Services

categories.name: Financial and Blockchain Services
categories.short_description: Financial transactions, market data access, and blockchain analysis.
categories.definition: Servers whose primary function is financial data, transactions, trading, payments, ecommerce operations, accounting, invoices, banking, cryptocurrency, wallets, smart contracts, tokens, NFTs, or blockchain/on-chain analysis.
include: Market and financial data: stocks, prices, portfolio, trading signals, exchanges, yFinance, Alpha Vantage, Tradovate
Trading and banking operations: place/cancel orders, account balances, banking transactions, invoices, accounting
Payments and ecommerce: Stripe, PayPal, Shopify, WooCommerce, products, carts, customers, orders, storefront operations
Blockchain and crypto: Ethereum, Bitcoin, Solana, Starknet, EVM, wallets, addresses, tokens, NFTs, smart contracts, transactions, blocks, on-chain analytics
Finance-specific AI/agent tools when exposed operations are finance, trading, payment, ecommerce, or blockchain oriented
exclude: Generic company/economic data retrieval without financial operation semantics
Blockchain or finance documentation retrieval without wallet, transaction, market, or smart-contract operations
Security scanning of smart contracts or crypto projects when vulnerability/security audit is dominant
Generic token, API token, auth token, or OAuth token setup
Repository operations for crypto projects
positive_examples: A Binance or yFinance server exposing price and portfolio tools
A Stripe server exposing create_payment and list_customers
A Shopify server exposing products, orders, and customers
An Ethereum wallet/on-chain analysis server exposing address and transaction tools
negative_examples: A database of public company profiles with read-only search: Data and Public Content Access
A smart-contract vulnerability scanner: Security, Access Control, and Scanning
A blockchain documentation RAG server: Data and Public Content Access
A GitHub repo manager for a crypto project: Source Control and Collaboration

categories.name: Analytics and Peripheral Tools
categories.short_description: Computational analysis, visualization, and peripheral interaction.
categories.definition: Servers whose primary function is computation, analysis, statistics, visualization, reporting, simulation, optimization, creative/media generation or editing, design tools, transcription, QR generation, hardware, camera, sensor, or other peripheral/tool utilities.
include: Math, statistics, symbolic computation, numeric computation, simulation, optimization, calculators
Data analysis and visualization: charts, plots, dashboards, reports, notebooks, spreadsheets, CSV/Excel processing
Media and creative tools: image, video, audio, music, TTS/STT, transcription, Figma, Blender, Unity, design, drawing, QR codes
Peripheral/hardware utilities: camera, OpenCV, sensors, IoT-style device interaction when not primarily infrastructure or security
AI generation/model wrappers when the main exposed output is generated media, text, analysis, transformation, or creative/computational output rather than data retrieval
exclude: Simple database, document, web, or public-content retrieval without meaningful computation/transformation
Financial/blockchain analytics with trading, wallet, payment, token, or on-chain semantics
Security analysis, vulnerability scanning, CVE lookup, pentesting, or compliance audit
Browser automation where UI control/screenshot/scraping is the primary operation
Repository code review, PR analysis, commit analysis, or source-control workflows
positive_examples: A calculator/statistics MCP server exposing compute and plot tools
A Figma/Blender/Unity server exposing design or scene editing tools
A TTS/transcription/audio server exposing media transformation tools
A QR/camera/OpenCV server exposing peripheral or image-processing tools
negative_examples: A SQL query server returning rows without analysis: Data and Public Content Access
A crypto market analytics server tied to wallets/trading: Financial and Blockchain Services
A CVE analysis or dependency vulnerability scanner: Security, Access Control, and Scanning
A Playwright screenshot/browser automation server: Local Execution and Automation

categories.name: Security, Access Control, and Scanning
categories.short_description: Access control, security auditing, and scanning.
categories.definition: Servers whose primary function is vulnerability scanning, security auditing, penetration testing, threat intelligence, CVE analysis, IAM, identity, secrets, permissions, policies, compliance, access control, or security-focused audit of systems, repositories, dependencies, infrastructure, or applications.
include: Vulnerability scanning, dependency scanning, CVE lookup, threat intelligence, pentesting, exploit/security assessment
Network/security scanning: Nmap, port scanning, host discovery, fingerprinting, web security scanning
Identity and access control: IAM, permissions, roles, users, groups, access policies, Lake Formation, Keycloak, authz management
Secrets and policy management: vaults, secret scanning, credential audit, compliance checks, policy-as-code
Security-focused repository, browser extension, infrastructure, cloud, package, or smart-contract audit
exclude: Generic OAuth/API key configuration needed to call another service
General GitHub/GitLab repository operations without security/audit focus
General infrastructure operations without security/audit/compliance objective
Local filesystem tools with names like secure or safe but no security scanning/access-control capability
Financial/blockchain services unless the exposed operation is security scanning or audit
positive_examples: An Nmap MCP server exposing port_scan and host_discovery
A Vault/secrets MCP server exposing read_secret and create_policy
A Snyk/dependency scanner exposing scan_project and vulnerability reports
An IAM or permission audit server exposing list_roles and access_audit
negative_examples: A Gmail server requiring OAuth: Task and Schedule Management
A GitHub server creating pull requests: Source Control and Collaboration
A Cloudflare server managing DNS and certificates without audit focus: Infrastructure and Gateway Services
A filesystem server named secure but only reading/writing files: Local Execution and Automation

llm_output_schema.decision_basis: short explanation grounded in provided evidence
evidence: short evidence snippets or tool names used for the decision
llm_output_schema.ambiguity_notes: short note if evidence is sparse or categories are close
